match.detail: a label that wraps a control or a Field card is Field composition*

entries.reason: The recipe build lists each declaration of an arm the definition omits by hand. The capture lists each class that won nothing in any cell once, under `no rule of the class wins`.

match.detail: a marker class with no CSS

entries.reason: A marker class wins no declaration, so the capture lists it with the classes that won nothing.

match.detail: no rule of the class wins a declaration on an element of any captured cell

entries.reason: Each class of the label and its Field root that styles nothing in either cell, found by the browser instead of listed by hand.
The recipe build models the docs body by hand; the capture reads the host page's body rule and binds the same variables.
The body rule the page renders, binding `foreground` and `font-sans` as before.

In the browser the Field root's `[&>:where(…)]:w-full` (0,1,0) beats the label's `w-fit` (0,1,0) by source order, so the label is 100% wide; the recipe cascade never saw the Field root. Both hug in the spec, since the root sits alone.
The Field root's child rule that wins the label's width, as above.
The shipped `styles.css` writes `gap: .5rem`; both read as 8px.
The shipped `styles.css` writes `opacity: .5`; both map to opacity 0.5.
The rest of Fuse's base layer, which the recipe cascade did not model: box sizing, zero border, margin and padding.
Tailwind's preflight, which the capture page loads as the docs host does.
The browser's default style for `<label>`, which the recipe cascade did not model.
